title: State of AI Readiness: Launch Edition 2026
honestFraming: The score measures AI readiness: crawler access and on-page signals. It does not measure whether any assistant names or cites a site.

findings.headline: The typical site scores 73 out of 100.
findings.body: The mean is 73 and the median 75. The middle half of the 219 scored sites sit between 67 and 82, and the range runs from 30 to 100.

findings.headline: B2B software scored higher than consumer categories, 76 against 69.
findings.body: In this sample the three B2B software categories (125 sites) average 76.4 and the three consumer-facing ones (94 sites) 68.6, a gap of 7.8 points. Differences of a point or two between single categories are not worth reading into.

findings.headline: The most common gap is homepage content schema, missing from 76.7% of sites.
findings.body: No Article, FAQ, Product or similar type on the homepage. The scan reads only the homepage, so a missing type there is not by itself a defect. It is where the most points were left on the table.

findings.headline: 14 of 219 sites (6.4%) block at least one of ten tracked AI crawlers outright.
findings.body: One site blocks all ten. For most sites, an ordinary Disallow rule on a path is what applies to AI crawlers, which is a limit, not a block.

method: 219 hand-picked, well-known websites in six categories: CRM software, cybersecurity, DevTools and cloud, DTC brands, consumer apps, and hospitality and travel.
One scan of each homepage and its public files (robots.txt, llms.txt, the sitemap), with the 16 checks of the public methodology: discoverability 40 points, technical 20, content and trust 40.
CRM software and DTC brands were scanned on 29 July 2026, the other four categories on 31 July. 278 sites were attempted; the 59 that could not be scored (21.2%) are left out of every figure.
limits: Presence in AI answers. The scan measures readiness, not what an assistant says. No number links to citations, answers or traffic.
The web, or an industry. The sites are hand-picked, so "sites in our sample" is the widest claim the numbers support. There are no confidence intervals or significance claims.
Cause and effect. A check is worth some points on our scale. That says nothing about what fixing it changes outside the score.
A trend. Each site was scanned once, on three days in July. Nothing here is rising or falling.
Sites that could not be read. 59 of 278 are missing from every figure, 43 because robots.txt could not be read. The averages describe sites our scanner could read.
